lessons: Psalm references: the Indonesian Catholic Bible (TB + Deuterokanonika) counts the Psalm heading as verse 1, so the verse number is often one higher than in RSV/NAB. Vulg. 35:10 'in lumine tuo videbimus lumen' = Mzm 36:10, not 36:9. Always check the verse text in qNNN.ayat.json and never convert Vulgate numbers by the Hebrew chapter shift alone.
Augustine book numbers in the 1920 English are unreliable ('ultimo de civ. Dei' = xxii; 'ultimo de Trin.' = xv; Gen. ad lit. 'xiii' does not exist). Take the book number from the Latin.
Watch the scope of the negation in 'Non ergo quicumque ... vident omnia' ('not everyone who ... sees all'). The English 'whosoever ... does not know all' makes it a universal negative.
In 'haec non removentur ab eo propter eius defectum' (a12), 'haec' means the predicates denied of God (via remotionis), not the creatures.
'Insecutio' in the comprehensio distinction (a7 ad 1) is 'mengejar', which ties back to 'sequor' in Flp 3:12. The English 'non-attainment' loses this.

imago in the sense of a portrait (a9 resp 'in sua imagine'; ad 2 'similitudine imaginis') was left as 'gambar'. The owner's imago → citra decision is recorded for imago Dei. Extending it to portraits should be decided explicitly before q.35 and q.93.

glossary_proposals.alasan: Keeps the link to Flp 3:12 'sequor' in the broad sense of comprehensio as one of the dotes of the soul.

The glossary row for imago covers imago Dei only. Thomas uses the portrait analogy (a man known 'in sua imagine') precisely to explain imago later, so the owner should decide whether one word covers both.
glossary_proposals.rujukan: STh I q.12 a.9 resp. dan ad 2; I q.35, q.93
